node-1.label: A 19-year-old male presents with headache described as blurred vision when hearing noise, followed by intermittent tingling at the top of the head, lasting about 5 minutes and occurring 5-6 times a day for the past 5 months

node-2.label: Past history includes encephalitis with high fever at age 5, followed by seizures at age 9; seizures were well-controlled with medication for the past 7 years

node-3.label: Patient became irritable with suicidal intentions a year ago and was diagnosed with anxiety disorder

node-4.label: Born at term with home delivery, normal physical growth (height 172.4 cm, weight 97.3 kg), no family history of mental illness or genetic disorders

node-5.label: Physical examination: right-handed male with symmetrical face and limbs, no abnormal walking gait; MMSE score 21 indicating mild mental retardation

why.why: Past encephalitis with subsequent seizures, cognitive impairment, normal physical examination, and absence of genetic predisposition are now strongly reinforced by CT/MRI showing right cerebral hemisphere atrophy and encephalomalacia in the right frontal and temporal lobes, plus EEG showing right temporal slow waves without epileptiform discharges. These findings confirm prior encephalitis scarring and residual organic dysfunction rather than active epilepsy. Confidence is 0.85 because CSF/serology and formal neuropsychological assessment were not obtained.

The headache pattern and normal examination initially suggested migraine, but CT/MRI demonstrating right hemisphere atrophy and encephalomalacia plus EEG showing right temporal slow waves indicate an acquired structural sequelae, making migraine an unlikely primary explanation.

Although anxiety disorder was diagnosed a year ago and physical examination is normal, the significant organic history and now-confirmed structural and EEG abnormalities (right hemisphere atrophy/encephalomalacia, right temporal slow waves) make anxiety/somatoform disorder much less likely to be the primary cause.

Imaging shows right hemisphere atrophy and encephalomalacia rather than a space-occupying mass, and EEG shows no epileptiform discharges; these findings are consistent with post-encephalitic scarring and exclude a large focal lesion. Normal neurological examination and lack of genetic predisposition further reduce the likelihood of an intracranial space-occupying lesion.

node-10.label: CT and MRI show right cerebral hemisphere atrophy and encephalomalacia in the right frontal and temporal lobes

node-11.label: EEG shows right temporal slow waves without epileptiform discharges

node-12.label: Episodes are active focal seizures originating from the right temporal lobe

attrs.why: The brief stereotyped episodes of visual blurring and tingling and the history of prior encephalitis with seizures could suggest active focal seizures. However, seizures have been well-controlled for 7 years, and EEG shows right temporal slow waves without epileptiform discharges, making active epilepsy unlikely. Confidence remains low.
